Examination revealed impaired adduction, restricted upward gaze and intorsion with down gaze bilaterally, consistent with partial cranial nerve III palsies. Direct and consensual pupillary responses were normal. His bedside forced vital capacity was 2.2 L. His GBS disability rating score was 3.

He also received supportive care with topical lubricating eye drops, eye patches and an indwelling catheter after developing urinary retention. He underwent 4 weeks of inpatient rehabilitation for persistent gait difficulties and lower limb weakness.

report.source_text: At 6 weeks after onset of symptoms, the patient’s ophthalmoplegia and ataxia have resolved and he has minimal residual bilateral facial weakness. He has persistent bilateral proximal lower limb weakness (Medical Research Council grade 4). The patient has returned home, is living independently and is ambulating with a four-wheel frame.

clinician.final_diagnosis: MFS-GBS overlap syndrome associated with the Oxford-AstraZeneca SARS-CoV2 vaccination
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 63-year-old man developed new onset severe bilateral facial weakness, unsteadiness, lower limb weakness and paraesthesia 14 days after his first Oxford-AstraZeneca vaccine dose. He presented with sensory ataxia, facial diplegia involving the forehead, proximal lower limb weakness, areflexia, and impaired proprioception. CSF analysis revealed albuminocytologic dissociation with markedly elevated protein and no pleocytosis. MRI brain showed bilateral facial and oculomotor nerve enhancement consistent with cranial nerve involvement. Nerve conduction studies showed chronic axonal neuropathy without acute demyelination. Serum anti-GQ1b antibody was negative. During admission, he developed partial bilateral cranial nerve III palsies and diplopia. He was treated with a 5-day course of IVIG and underwent 4 weeks of inpatient rehabilitation. At 6 weeks post symptom onset, ophthalmoplegia and ataxia resolved with minimal residual facial weakness, and he ambulates with assistive support at home. The clinical presentation, supportive CSF and imaging findings, exclusion of alternate infectious causes, negative anti-GQ1b antibody, and temporal relation to vaccination support the diagnosis of MFS-GBS overlap syndrome post Oxford-AstraZeneca SARS-CoV2 vaccination.
